discovery: Discovery of quantized conductance in ballistic one-dimensional semiconductor constrictions

nominees.name: Michael Pepper
nominees.affiliation: University College London and University of Cambridge, United Kingdom

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic quantum transport
motivation: In 1988 the Cambridge group led by Michael Pepper and, independently, the Delft-Philips team including Bart van Wees found that the conductance of a narrow, gate-defined constriction in a GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron gas rises in steps of 2e²/h. This was the first direct observation that electrical conductance through a nanoscale channel is quantized by its number of transverse modes. It is a striking, universal macroscopic signature of electron waves and it confirmed the Landauer picture of transport. The quantum point contact became a basic tool of mesoscopic physics. It underpins charge sensing and single-electron readout in semiconductor quantum dots and spin qubits, and it opened decades of work on one-dimensional physics, including the 0.7 anomaly. These are precise, reproducible experiments at the fundamental limits of fabrication, and they turned quantum transport into an engineering platform for quantum technology.
